da-false-claim.notes: The two PROVED claims (parts 1 and 2 of the .md) are mathematically true and correctly formalized.

da-vacuous.evidence: delta-pre-archimedean.md:36-44 — part 1 ('fold commutes with subtraction') is, as the .md itself states, 'a one-line consequence of additivity over a generic commutative ring'. fold_commutes_sub is genuine but elementary (it is just additivity ⇒ map_sub, already in Mathlib as map_sub for AddMonoidHom). The proposition's mathematical content is a restatement of a standard fact; the substance is the physics interpretation, not the lemma.
da-vacuous.notes: Not vacuous in the ': True' sense, but the formal theorems are near-trivial (map_sub for additive maps; squaring is nonlinear). Flagged minor: the load-bearing content is interpretive, the Lean is an elementary exercise.

da-circular.notes: No back-fitting: the proposition is a pure algebra fact about additive maps and a counterexample for nonlinear maps; no calibration or target value is assumed.

da-overclaim.evidence: delta-pre-archimedean.md:84-88 — 'Computing the absolute masses first and subtracting would interleave the nonlinear τ with the subtraction, breaking fold-invariance and (empirically) over-amplifying the split by ∼10².' The ~10² over-amplification is an empirical/physical claim presented as the consequence of the proved non-commutation, but the proved theorem only shows τ(xn)−τ(xp)≠τ(xn−xp) for SOME nonlinear τ (squaring over ℤ) — it does not establish that the actual archimedean functor over-amplifies Δ_pn by 10². The general claim is much stronger than the single witnessed inequality.
da-overclaim.notes: The headline physics payoff ('~10² over-amplification') is asserted from a generic non-commutation lemma whose only witness is squaring over ℤ; the quantitative 10² is not derived or witnessed here. Part 3 is honestly flagged as 'expository convention', but the 10² consequence is stated as fact.

da-hidden-dof.notes: No free parameter introduced; the proposition is parameter-free algebra.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: delta-pre-archimedean.md:77-88 — 'By (1) those folds commute … By (2) the same folds would not commute with the difference of two τ-images. Hence: Folding/unfolding works for binding precisely because binding is a pre-archimedean delta.' The 'precisely because' / 'hence' asserts that pre-archimedean-ness is the REASON folding is valid, but (1)+(2) only establish that fold commutes with fibre-subtraction and that τ does not commute with subtraction — they do not by themselves prove the binding observable is computed in the delta-then-τ order (that is conceded as 'expository convention' in part 3). The 'hence' slightly oversells (1)+(2) into justifying the modelling choice.
da-non-sequitur.notes: The logical bridge from the two lemmas to 'folding works BECAUSE binding is pre-archimedean' relies on the (admittedly conventional) choice that binding IS a pre-archimedean delta; the .md is careful to flag this as convention (part 3), so minor.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: cites kassel1995 (.ts:13); the lib file -- Ref: [kassel1995] for the Hecke antipode σ↦σ⁻¹ being an additive/ring map (FibreFold instance). Kassel's 'Quantum Groups' does cover the Hecke algebra antipode/bar involution. Appropriate.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: delta-pre-archimedean.md:13-15 — 'any fibre fold — the bar involution, the Hecke antipode, or a Type-B fold — i.e. any additive map on the fibre coefficient ring'. The bar involution q↦q⁻¹ and the Hecke antipode σ↦σ⁻¹ are ring/anti-homomorphisms, not merely additive on a single coefficient ring; subsuming all three under 'additive map' (the only property FibreFold captures, lean:64-67) is a simplification that conflates distinct structures. 'fibre coefficient ring' is not pinned to a specific ring in the .md.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: 'Fold' is defined as 'additive map' for the proof's convenience, but the three named examples carry more (multiplicative) structure; the base ring is left generic in prose. Minor ambiguity, intentional for the lemma.

da-empirical-fragility.evidence: delta-pre-archimedean.md:88 — '(empirically) over-amplifying the split by ∼10²'. This lone empirical number is stated without a witness, error bar, or q₀-anchor; it is the only quantitative claim and is not backed by any computation in this block.
da-empirical-fragility.notes: The ~10² figure is an unwitnessed empirical aside; not central to the proved proposition but stated as fact. No fit-noise issue since nothing is fitted here, hence minor.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: The order-of-operations discipline (form the categorical difference before applying the nonlinear archimedean functor) is physically/methodologically sound; no conservation or unit violation.

da-reproducibility.notes: No witness/computation attached; the claims are Lean-proved (fold_commutes_sub, archimedean_does_not_commute_sub) and verifiable by lean-direct. The single empirical ~10² aside is the only unwitnessed value (covered under da-empirical-fragility).

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: accept-with-minor-revision. referee_argument: This is the strongest block of the five — it carefully separates two genuinely-proved, correctly-formalized facts (fold commutes with fibre subtraction; the nonlinear archimedean functor does not) from an explicitly-flagged expository convention. The proved Lean content is elementary (essentially map_sub plus a squaring counterexample) but honest. The one weakness is the unwitnessed '∼10² over-amplification' physics claim (md:88), which is asserted as the consequence of a generic non-commutation lemma whose only witness is squaring over ℤ; it should be witnessed or softened. Also tighten the 'any fold = any additive map' identification, which drops the multiplicative structure of the named examples.
